newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler unit forms Internet commerce firm.
newsitem.headline: Daimler unit forms Internet commerce firm.

text.p: Debis Systemhaus, a unit of Daimler-Benz Interservices AG, said on Friday it had formed a company to help enterprises conduct business over the Internet, the global computer network.

The new company, to be called Systemhaus Internet Business Services GmbH, will provide access to the Internet, business data integration services, business applications for the World Wide Web, the popular graphical part of the Internet, as well as operate computer servers and networks.
The company will focus on industries such as commerce, financial services, tourism, publishing and media.

The company said online services such as CompuServe and America Online generated transaction revenues of $500 million in Europe last year and predicted this would rise to more than $1.2 billion by the year 2000.

Equipped with a modem, consumers can use a personal computer to connect to an online service over a normal phone line and can order books, music CDs, make hotel reservations and use other services from home or at work.
The managing director of the the new company is Juergen Becker, 39, former director of Luxembourg-based online service Europe Online S.A.
